diagnosis.root_cause: The OLT health check has a contradictory status rule: it reports the OLT as healthy while seven of eight PONs are marked failed, and the live probe shows all tested ONUs on EPON0/7 are definite offline responses. The OLT itself is reachable by ping and SNMP, so this is not an OLT failure; the health-check classification is defective while concealing a substantial PON outage.
evidence: The target ONU has onu_status 0, and the live ONU probe responds true with online 0, MPCP DEREG, and no optical readings; this is a definite offline state, not a missing-monitoring response.
All eight tested ONUs on EPON0/7 return responds true and online 0, so the affected port has no surviving ONUs and meets the whole-port-down condition for a PON-port outage.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, its OID subtree responds, and its CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are near healthy baselines; therefore the OLT itself is not failed.
The stored OLT detail marks seven of eight PONs as failed while overall_status is healthy. A healthy summary concealing all or all-but-one failed PONs is a health-check/status-rule defect.
The direct online values establish real service impact beneath the monitoring defect; the affected scope is therefore OLT-level rather than single-customer.

The customer's optical telemetry before the final data gap was stable: RX stayed around -21.1 to -21.7 dBm, TX around +2.3 dBm, distance remained 166, and TX bias stayed near 11 mA. There is no evidence of fibre degradation, laser degradation, or distance change.
The VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1047, the RADIUS record is present and CRM-consistent, the router heartbeat is healthy, and one session in the last 24 hours is not flapping.

remediation.action: Immediately correct the OLT health-check status logic and open network-impacting incidents for the failed PONs. Investigate and restore EPON0/7, where all eight tested ONUs are definitely offline, then validate the other seven reported failed PONs individually. Do not replace or reboot the OLT solely on this evidence: CPU, memory, temperature, ping, SNMP, and uptime are healthy. Suppress the misleading healthy result until per-PON status agrees with live ONU probes.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check marks an OLT critical only when every sampled PON fails. Seven of eight failed here, so it wrote 'healthy' with a null error description while healthy_pons stood at 1 of 8 in the same record. A genuine multi-port outage is running underneath a healthy verdict.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports overall_status healthy with a null error description
The same record holds healthy_pons 1 against total_pons_tested 8, and seven entries in failed_pons_list
The summary label contradicts the detail fields inside one record
The check sets critical only when every sampled PON fails, so seven of eight yields healthy by design
Probing confirms every ONU on EPON0/7 returns responds true with online 0, a definite negative
oid_subtree_responds is true, so this is not the firmware mismatch mechanism
43 of 272 customers on the OLT are offline, far above the 4.85% background rate
Sessions ended together and PON traffic has collapsed from 219 to 6 Mbps
This is a genuine multi-port outage that the health check's status rule conceals

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check reported healthy during a seven-port outage; the status rule needs correcting

distractors: The health record says healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
A scheduled scan with no complaint gives no reason to look harder
The fault type is a health check defect but the service impact is real
